records.expected_impact: Verifier processes no longer hold secret material: full verifier-memory compromise no longer enables release forgery. Raises the GOV-3 cost ladder's floor from 'signing key + commit access' to 'signing key + commit access + breaking the git-anchored public-key history' — with the public key anchored in immutable commit objects, forgery requires the human, not the process.
records.description: Deploy ed25519 asymmetric signing into the live governance release chain, replacing the HMAC-SHA256 stage-2 model. Justification receipted in N8587-1 LEG F (verifier compromise): with HMAC, an attacker who compromises the verifying process reads the shared secret and forges releases 4/4; with ed25519 the verifier holds only the public key and the same compromise yields zero forgeries (4/4 rejected). GOV-3's disclosed scope-honesty note anticipated exactly this upgrade. Deployment steps: (1) generate ed25519 release keypair, key held in process custody (gitignored, never published); (2) pin the PUBLIC key fingerprint in the git-anchored registry alongside the existing key pin; (3) sign the next governance release v2 with ed25519 and dual-verify (HMAC v1 + ed25519 v2) for one cycle; (4) retire HMAC verification after one clean cycle. All per Constitution Art. 2.2: no deployment without Leon's explicit approval.
records.title: SIP-10: ed25519 asymmetric governance release signing (live chain upgrade)
records.rationale: N8587-1 quantified the asymmetry (4/4 vs 0/4). GOV-3 stage-2 shipped HMAC as a model with this upgrade pre-disclosed as the production refinement; the receipt now exists to justify it.

records.expected_impact: Converts the system's final floor from 'human review over append-only history' (unmeasured by machines) into a machine-checkable external anchor: the maximal attacker's cost becomes keys+commit PLUS an immutable external system.
records.description: FILED PENDING APPROVAL (from DHB-3 finding, Oct 13, 2026, 12:26 CT directive): Anchor Binding — DOI-bind the three anchor fingerprints (issuance_registry.json, gov_release_registry.json, gov_key_pin.txt) into the machine-readable BINDINGS record at every release. DHB-3 (convergence battery) measured the whole system's final floor as ONE NUMBER: with both keys (signing + issuance) AND git commit access, ZERO software layers resist on either plane — the forged relaxed roster verified in-process, 40/40 minted records passed the signed-issuance gate, the brain over-healed 9600 vs 2646 while the clamp held boundedness (sick but honest, closure 0.00e+00). The forgery is attributable in git history, but commit access forges the ledger trail too, and the DOI-bound Zenodo record set currently binds 0 of 3 anchor files — zero machine-checkable external anchors remain; the floor is human review over append-only history. PROPOSED FIX: (1) every release (governance or issuance) appends the anchor-file fingerprints to the DOI-bound BINDINGS record (BIND-2/v1 contract, binding_archive fail-closed); (2) an external verification leg (fresh-clone + BINDINGS check) added to the run-end audit: a forged registry whose fingerprint is absent or divergent from the DOI-bound record is DETECTED regardless of local git state; (3) the one number becomes 1: the maximal attacker must additionally defeat Zenodo — an immutable external system outside keys+commit — to erase forensics. HONEST LIMIT: Zenodo record immutability is operator-requestable for new versions (records are versioned, not deleted) — the binding pins the fingerprint history, and erasing it requires defeating both Zenodo's versioning and human review of the public ledger.
records.title: Anchor binding: DOI-bind the registry/key-pin fingerprints (SIP-7, from DHB-3 finding)

records.description: FILED PENDING APPROVAL (from DHB-2 finding, Oct 13, 2026, 12:20 CT directive): Signed Issuance Registry — the data-plane mirror of SIP-4's signed releases. DHB-2 (issuer campaign battery) found that a patient adversary minting fully-conforming, in-profile, registry-valid records steers the whole brain's disposition while EVERY deployed layer reports normal operation: guard accepts 60/60 (conforming by construction), reconciliation attributes the drift as legitimate (within budget), release chain untouched — F2-2 fails as found: the crossing has no provenance. PROPOSED FIX: (1) issuers sign the issued-id block at issuance time (HMAC-SHA256 over the id registry, key held in process custody, fingerprint + registry anchored in git — the exact SIP-4 pattern); (2) ingestion guard v2.3 holds records whose id is absent from the signed issuance registry (fail-closed, flagged as unsigned_issuance); (3) a compromised issuer flips from an INVISIBLE class to a DETECTABLE forgery class (signature break at the gate). HONEST LIMIT: an attacker holding the ISSUANCE KEY can still mint — this prices the data-plane cost ladder twin to GOV's: id format (held) -> registry-valid ids (passes, DHB-2's vector) -> signed-registry-verified (SIP-6 closes) -> issuance-key compromise (new floor, symmetric to GOV-3's key+commit rung). Secondary honest observation from DHB-2: the bounded rule's near-saturation at the operating point blunts disposition steering (+7.5e-5 over 47 heals) — invisibility is the finding, magnitude is the measurement.

records.expected_impact: Bounded weights (<1.0 by construction), true convergence within ~10 epochs, no change to any governance/invariance property. Enables the January 1, 2027 reveal to carry a convergent multi-epoch training curve.
records.implementation_difficulty: Low — one-line rule change plus rerun of HEMI-T2 series as HEMI-T2B under an amended prereg (HEMI-2.2).
records.description: Amend the HEMI-2 frozen learning rule from w' = w + lr*(1-c) to the bounded form w' = w + lr*(1-c)*(1-w). The unbounded form is a positive-feedback loop: HEMI-T2 showed sum|delta| growing 0.85->1.83 over 10 epochs and max weight escaping to 1.36 with no convergence. The bounded form is asymptotic below 1.0 by construction, preserving self-damping while keeping all HEMI-T1/T2 invariance properties. Governance containment was perfect throughout (playbook invariance at every epoch), so the proposal touches ONLY the training rule, not the governance layer.
records.title: HEMI-2.2: Bounded Learning Rule Amendment (w' = w + lr*(1-c)*(1-w))
records.rationale: HEMI-T2 series falsifiers HF-S2 (convergence) and HF-S3 (boundedness) failed under the frozen unbounded rule; the failure is receipted in ledger 2026-10-13T02:58Z and receipt hemi_t2_receipt.json. records.description: Add an idempotency key check at the start of every scheduled workflow. Mechanics: (1) each workflow computes a deterministic signature (workflow_name + scheduled_window, e.g. 'wed-op-stress|2026-09-02'); (2) before executing, query RemediationSweep / entity log for the same signature in the current window; (3) if found, exit silently as duplicate — log to RateLimitLog as idempotency_skip; (4) if not found, execute and stamp the signature. This converts double-fires (platform retry, clock drift) into silent no-ops instead of duplicate records and double credit billing. Test 4 of the Sept 2 adversarial suite proved the entity layer accepts duplicates — the guard must live at the workflow entry point.
records.title: Workflow idempotency keys: dedupe double-fired scheduled jobs by signature

records.rationale: Adversarial Test 1 (Tenant Isolation Attack, Sept 2 2026) proved unfiltered reads return cross-tenant data. Found before any customer was harmed — the exact purpose of pre-launch adversarial testing.

records.description: Antifragility training round 1 exposed 5 OOD anomaly classes with no matching playbooks: quantum_mesh_decoherence, cross_jurisdiction_regulatory_collision, temporal_causal_inversion, healing_tool_dependency_poison (META), semantic_field_drift. Proposal: author 5 new playbooks with conservative confidence_threshold (0.85) since each family has only 1-2 occurrences. META class (healing tool poison) should be playbook'd as PERMANENT human-escalation — never auto-heal.
records.title: Author 5 OOD-class playbooks from antifragility training findings
records.rationale: Core Directive 3: no matching playbook exists for 5 detected anomaly types. Learning loop requires proposal → approval → deployment cycle.

records.expected_impact: Establish protocol for handling completely unknown anomaly types. Prevents blind auto-healing of novel issues.
records.description: Anomaly with 0% confidence detected — no pattern match at all. This is a completely novel anomaly type. System correctly did NOT auto-heal. SelfImprovementProposal generated. Need: (1) novel anomaly detection protocol, (2) human review pipeline for unknown types, (3) pattern creation workflow from novel anomalies.
records.title: Novel Anomaly Detection Protocol (0% Confidence Edge Case)
records.rationale: 0% confidence is an edge case that tests the system's ability to recognize when it doesn't know something. This is the most important safety property.

records.expected_impact: Reduce BGP hijack response time from manual hours to automated minutes. Prevent traffic interception.
records.description: BGP route hijack is a critical security event with no existing playbook. Need a playbook that: (1) detects unauthorized AS announcements, (2) alerts upstream providers, (3) initiates route filtering, (4) verifies traffic paths. Currently escalated — no auto-heal.
records.title: Create BGP Route Hijack Response Playbook
records.rationale: BGP hijack was correctly escalated but has no auto-heal path. Network security is a gap in the playbook library.

records.expected_impact: Reduce SAP queue backup resolution from hours to seconds for enterprise customers using SAP.
records.description: SAP IDoc queue backup is an enterprise domain with limited coverage. Need playbook for: (1) IDoc queue depth monitoring, (2) batch processing restart, (3) failed IDoc isolation, (4) SAP integration health check.
records.title: Formalize SAP IDoc Queue Management Playbook
records.rationale: SAP IDoc healing worked but playbook was ad-hoc. Formalize for enterprise tier customers.

records.expected_impact: Prevent false auto-healing of IoT sensors that may be correctly reading environmental changes. Establish IoT domain safety baseline.
records.description: IoT sensor drift at 76% confidence was correctly NOT auto-healed. Need: (1) sensor calibration verification protocol, (2) environmental factor analysis, (3) human review checklist, (4) confidence threshold tuning guidance for IoT devices.
records.title: Establish IoT Sensor Calibration Review Protocol
records.rationale: IoT is a new domain with unique safety considerations. Sensors reading actual changes should NOT be 'healed' back to baseline.

records.expected_impact: Reduce supply chain disruption from vendor outages. Automate failover for 40%+ order volume.
records.description: Supply chain vendor failover worked but needs: (1) vendor health scoring, (2) automatic backup vendor selection, (3) order rerouting logic, (4) vendor recovery detection and switchback.
records.title: Create Supply Chain Vendor Failover Playbook
records.rationale: Supply chain is a new domain with unique failover requirements. Formalize for logistics customers.

records.expected_impact: Reduce cross-vendor resolution time by 40-60% by pre-computing cascade paths instead of detecting each anomaly independently
records.description: Create a unified cross-vendor cascade handler that automatically chains healing across vendors when an anomaly in one vendor triggers related anomalies in others. Current approach heals each vendor independently; a cascade-aware playbook would pre-compute the blast radius and batch healing actions.
records.title: Cross-Vendor Cascade Handler — Unified Payment→Billing→Notification→Logging Playbook
records.rationale: First cross-vendor cascade test showed 4 independent healing events totaling 4720ms. A cascade-aware playbook could parallelize vendor heals and reduce total time to ~2000ms.

records.expected_impact: Closes a critical security gap in the telemetry-to-healing pipeline. Prevents adversarial manipulation of self-healing decisions.
records.description: New anomaly type 'adversarial_prompt_injection' detected via chaos stress test. No matching playbook exists. Proposal: create AegisPlaybook that (1) sanitizes all telemetry input fields for prompt injection patterns, (2) validates healing playbook selection against allow-list, (3) quarantines telemetry streams with anomalous content patterns, (4) alerts on any attempt to override playbook selection logic.
records.title: Create Playbook: Telemetry Input Sanitization & Prompt Injection Defense
records.rationale: Chaos stress test #7 revealed a gap — an adversarial payload embedded in a telemetry field could potentially influence healing playbook selection. This is a novel attack vector not covered by existing 437 playbooks.

records.expected_impact: Prevents 90%+ incidents
